issues.failure_explanation: The least squares operator maps into the m-dimensional space V_m. Its worst-case error over the unit ball is therefore at least the error at f = varphi_{m+1}/sigma_{m+1}, which is sigma_{m+1}^{-1} = d_m. In (ii) and (iii), m = n. Take sigma_s^{-1} constant up to s = n+1 and negligible afterwards; this is allowed for a non-decreasing sigma with sigma^{-1} in l_2. Then sum_{s>=n} d_s^2 is about d_n^2, so the right-hand side is about d_n/sqrt(n) (or d_n*sqrt(log n/n)), which is below d_n <= LHS. In (i) the tail starts at n/log n, which exceeds m = floor(n/(20 log n)), so the RHS can lie far below d_m. The cited results carry universal multiplicative constants and shifted tail indices; these are dropped here. The statement also claims all n, while Assumption points needs n>=90.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bounds as C*sqrt((log n/n) sum_{s>=c n/log n} d_s^2), C*sqrt((log n/n) sum_{s>=c n} d_s^2) and C*sqrt((1/n) sum_{s>=c n} d_s^2), with universal C, c as in the cited theorems, and restrict to n>=90.

issues.failure_explanation: varrho_n is an infimum over algorithms using at most n points, but S_{c_3n} uses c_3 n > n points. The definition yields only varrho_{c_3 n} <= sup||v - S_{c_3n}v||, and varrho_n >= varrho_{c_3n} goes the wrong way. With block-constant sigma^{-1} whose blocks have rapidly growing lengths, varrho_n >= d_n can exceed the c_3 n-point error by an unbounded factor. So 'varrho_n \ll sup||v - S_{c_3n}v||' is unjustified and false in general.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace varrho_n by varrho_{c_3 n} in the chain, or apply the result with floor(n/c_3) in place of n to get varrho_n \ll MN n^{-1/q}.

issues.failure_explanation: For s = s e_1 with s >= eta, sigma_s^2 = sum_{k<=eta} binom(s,k) rho_1^{2k} <= (eta+1) s^eta max(1, rho_1)^{2eta}. Hence sigma_{s e_1}^{-q} >= C s^{-eta q/2}, and ||sigma^{-1}||_{l_q}^q >= sum_s sigma_{s e_1}^{-q} = infinity whenever eta*q <= 2. In the regime q < 2 used downstream, eta = 1 always fails, so 'for any eta' is false. The cited summability result needs eta > 2/q.

issues.failure_explanation: The factor c_{s}^{a,b} is never defined, so sigma and the claim ||sigma^{-1}||_{l_q} <= N are not well defined. The hypotheses allow any positive rho with rho^{-1} in l_q, so finitely many rho_j may be < 1, which suits the smallness condition. Membership of sigma^{-1} in l_q forces sigma_{s e_j} = c_s^{a,b} rho_j^s -> infinity as s -> infinity, which fails for rho_j < 1 unless c_s grows exponentially. The analogous holomorphic lemma explicitly assumes rho_j > 1, which is absent here.
